clinical.citation: A de novo missense variant in MIDEAS results in increased deacetylase activity of the MiDAC HDAC complex causing a neurodevelopmental syndrome (PMID: 41290615)

variants.description: p.Tyr654Ser (de novo heterozygous; cDNA notation not given in abstract)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Same de novo heterozygous missense variant in two unrelated individuals. Located in a conserved auto-inhibitory loop covering the deacetylase active site (cryoEM structure). Predicted to displace the loop and increase MiDAC deacetylase activity. Patient fibroblasts show gene expression changes reciprocal to those seen after rapid MiDAC degradation.

model_organism.citation: Bantscheff/Millard et al. 2020 - The MiDAC histone deacetylase complex is essential for embryonic development and has a unique multivalent structure (PMID: 32591534)
phenotypes: Late embryonic death, with a phenotype identical to Dnttip1 knockout mice

biological.citation: Clinical genetics/structural study 2025 - A de novo missense variant in MIDEAS results in increased deacetylase activity of the MiDAC HDAC complex causing a neurodevelopmental syndrome (PMID: 41290615)
biological.summary: Two unrelated individuals with a multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder (delayed speech, joint contractures, dysmorphism, gut dysmotility) carry the same de novo MIDEAS p.Tyr654Ser variant. CryoEM places Tyr654 in an auto-inhibitory loop covering the HDAC active site, so the variant is proposed to displace the loop and raise MiDAC deacetylase activity. Patient fibroblasts show gene expression changes reciprocal to those seen after rapid MiDAC degradation.

biological.citation: 2020 - The MiDAC histone deacetylase complex is essential for embryonic development and has a unique multivalent structure (PMID: 32591534)
biological.summary: Mice lacking MIDEAS or DNTTIP1 die with identical late-embryonic phenotypes, including heart malformation and haematopoietic failure, linked to perturbed gene expression. MiDAC is also important for chromosome alignment in mitosis in cancer cell lines. The cryoEM structure shows four HDAC1 copies at the periphery with outward-facing active sites.

biological.citation: 2020 - The histone deacetylase complex MiDAC regulates a neurodevelopmental gene expression program to control neurite outgrowth (PMID: 32297854)
biological.summary: MiDAC regulates a neurodevelopmental gene expression program. It upregulates SLIT3 and NTN1, probably by removing H4K20ac at promoters and enhancers, and represses negative regulators of neurogenesis by reducing H3K27ac. MiDAC loss causes neurite outgrowth defects that SLIT3 and/or NTN1 supplementation rescues.

biological.citation: 2025 - Mutations on the surface of HDAC1 reveal molecular determinants of specific complex assembly and their requirement for gene regulation (PMID: 40966515)
biological.summary: Comparing the MIDEAS:HDAC1 and MTA1:HDAC1 structures identified HDAC1 surface residues needed for complex binding. The HDAC1 Y48E mutation disrupts binding to all complexes except SIN3. The E63R mutation markedly reduces binding to NuRD and MiDAC, and both mutants perturb gene expression and histone acetylation in cells.

biological.citation: 2015 - Structural and functional characterization of a cell cycle associated HDAC1/2 complex reveals the structural basis for complex assembly and nucleosome targeting (PMID: 25653165)
biological.summary: MIDEAS is a corepressor in a cell cycle-associated complex with HDAC1/2 and DNTTIP1 that is upregulated in mitosis and associated with cyclin A. The DNTTIP1 N-terminal dimerization domain mediates assembly of the HDAC1:MIDEAS complex. Its C-terminal domain binds DNA and nucleosomes, so DNTTIP1 acts as a dimeric chromatin-binding module.

biological.citation: 2024 - Mitotic deacetylase complex (MiDAC) recognizes the HIV-1 core promoter to control activated viral gene expression (PMID: 38781120)
biological.summary: DNA-affinity chromatography identified MiDAC as selectively recognizing the HIV core promoter TASHET element. DNTTIP1 binds TASHET directly and co-immunoprecipitates with MIDEAS and HDAC1/2. Gene silencing of MIDEAS, DNTTIP1 or NAT10 altered HIV expression in cells, implicating MIDEAS in Tat-activated transcription and latency.

biological.citation: 2023 - Long non-coding RNA MIDEAS-AS1 inhibits growth and metastasis of triple-negative breast cancer via transcriptionally activating NCALD (PMID: 37770991)
biological.summary: The antisense lncRNA MIDEAS-AS1 (not the MIDEAS protein) is downregulated in TNBC, and low levels correlate with poor OS and PFS. It interacts with MATR3 to activate NCALD transcription, which inactivates NF-κB signaling and suppresses tumor growth and metastasis.
biological.significance: correlated with poor OS and PFS (p-values not given in abstract)

biological.citation: 2025 - DNA methylation in peripheral blood leukocytes in late onset Alzheimer's disease (PMID: 40343304)
biological.summary: Differential methylation analysis of public blood datasets (GSE59685, GSE53740) listed MIDEAS among differentially methylated genes in late-onset Alzheimer's disease patients versus controls. This is an epigenetic association rather than a GWAS.
